name: TX-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's 24-point Republican partisan lean in deep-red East Texas
Incumbent Moran holds a roughly 70-to-1 fundraising edge ($2.4M vs $33K)
Prediction markets price a Republican win near 97%
No public polls or expert ratings; challenger has almost no cash
model.rationale: The district's 24-point Republican lean, Moran's incumbency and overwhelming fundraising advantage, and markets pricing a Republican win near certainty leave Prince without a visible path; fundamentals point to a margin of roughly 20 points for the incumbent.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending on Prince's behalf or unexpected polling showing a far tighter race would be the main things to watch, though nothing currently signals either.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-01 is a heavily Republican district in East Texas, with a partisan lean of about 24 points toward the GOP. Nathaniel Moran, the incumbent, is running for re-election after clearing his primary, and he has built a large financial advantage: roughly $2.4 million raised and about $960,000 on hand, with no outside spending against him. His Democratic opponent, Yolanda Prince, has raised about $33,000 and had roughly $8,000 in cash.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets put the Republican's chances near 97 percent. With the incumbent, the district's lean, and the fundraising gap all pointing the same direction, the Democratic side has no visible path to a competitive contest. A Republican win by roughly 20 points is the expected outcome, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any sign of a race.
